Pathfinder Toolkit › Conditions

All 43 conditions from Pathfinder Player Core and Player Core 2, in the Gazette's own short words. A condition with a value (frightened 2) gets worse as the number climbs, and two of the same take the higher value. To track them in a fight, open the ⚔️ Pathfinder Initiative Tracker.

Nothing by that name. Try fewer letters.

Seeing and being seen 6

  • Observed

    In plain view, or found by another precise sense. Hide and Sneak can turn it into hidden or undetected; Seek with only imprecise senses finds you hidden, not observed.

  • Concealed

    Hard to make out (fog, dim light). Anyone targeting you rolls a DC 5 flat check; on a failure the attack or effect misses you.

  • Hidden

    They know which square you're in but can't see you: you're off-guard to them, and they roll a DC 11 flat check to target you.

  • Undetected

    They don't know which square you're in: they have to guess, and even a right guess needs a DC 11 flat check.

  • Unnoticed

    They have no idea you're there. You're undetected too; some abilities work only on a foe who hasn't noticed you.

  • Invisible

    No one can see you: you're undetected until someone works out where you are, and hidden after that.

Senses 3

  • Blinded

    Can't see. What you could only see is undetected to you, Perception checks that need sight fail, other Perception checks take a −4 status penalty, and visual effects can't touch you.

  • Dazzled

    Your eyes are overwhelmed: everything you see is concealed to you.

  • Deafened

    Can't hear. Checks that need hearing fail, Perception for initiative and checks that mix sound with sight take a −2 status penalty, and auditory actions need a DC 5 flat check.

Death and dying 4

  • Dyingtakes a value

    At 0 HP, unconscious, and close to death. Roll a recovery check (flat check, DC 10 + the value) at the start of each turn. You die at dying 4, less your doomed value.

  • Woundedtakes a value

    You've come back from dying. The next time you're dying, add this value. Treat Wounds that heals you, or full HP and 10 minutes' rest, ends it.

  • Doomedtakes a value

    You die at dying 4 minus this value. It drops by 1 after a full night's rest.

  • Unconscious

    Asleep or knocked out: you can't act, you're blinded and off-guard, you take a −4 status penalty to AC, Perception, and Reflex saves, and you fall prone and drop what you hold.

Lowered abilities 4

  • Clumsytakes a value

    A status penalty equal to the value on Dexterity-based rolls and DCs: AC, Reflex saves, ranged attacks, Acrobatics, Stealth, and Thievery.

  • Drainedtakes a value

    A status penalty on Constitution-based rolls and DCs (Fortitude saves), and your HP and maximum HP drop by your level times the value. It drops by 1 after a full night's rest.

  • Enfeebledtakes a value

    A status penalty equal to the value on Strength-based rolls and DCs: melee attacks and their damage, and Athletics.

  • Stupefiedtakes a value

    A status penalty equal to the value on Intelligence-, Wisdom-, and Charisma-based rolls and DCs (Will saves, spell attacks and DCs), and casting a spell needs a DC 5 + value flat check.

Fear and the mind 5

  • Frightenedtakes a value

    A status penalty equal to the value on all checks and DCs. It drops by 1 at the end of each of your turns.

  • Fleeing

    You spend your actions getting away from the source, and you can't Delay or Ready.

  • Fascinated

    A −2 status penalty to Perception and skill checks, and no concentrate actions except about what holds your attention. Ends when anyone turns hostile toward you or your allies.

  • Confused

    Off-guard, no reactions, no Delay or Ready. You spend your actions attacking whoever the dice pick. Damage from an attack or spell gives a DC 11 flat check to snap out of it.

  • Controlled

    Someone else chooses your actions.

Actions 5

  • Quickened

    One extra action at the start of each turn, for whatever the effect allows.

  • Slowedtakes a value

    Lose this many actions at the start of each of your turns.

  • Stunnedtakes a value

    Lose this many actions as you regain them; each one lost lowers the value. A stun with a duration costs every action for that long instead.

  • Paralyzed

    Off-guard, and you can't act, apart from Recall Knowledge and other purely mental actions.

  • Petrified

    Turned to stone: you can't act or sense anything, and you count as an object.

The body 5

  • Fatigued

    A −1 status penalty to AC and saves, and no exploration activities while traveling. A full night's rest ends it.

  • Sickenedtakes a value

    A status penalty equal to the value on all checks and DCs, and you can't willingly eat or drink. Spend an action retching for a Fortitude save to lower it.

  • Encumbered

    Carrying too much: clumsy 1 and a 10-foot penalty to all your Speeds.

  • Persistent Damage

    Ongoing damage, such as burning: you take it again at the end of each of your turns, rerolling the dice, then roll a DC 15 flat check. A success ends it.

  • Curseboundtakes a value

    Oracles only: the price of leaning on your mystery. Your own oracular curse says what each value does to you. Only Refocusing clears it.

Holding and position 5

  • Off-Guard

    A −2 circumstance penalty to AC.

  • Prone

    On the ground: off-guard, a −2 circumstance penalty to attack rolls, and Crawl and Stand are your only move actions.

  • Grabbed

    Held in place: off-guard and immobilized, and a manipulate action needs a DC 5 flat check or it's lost.

  • Restrained

    Tied up or pinned: off-guard and immobilized, and no attack or manipulate actions except to Escape or Force Open.

  • Immobilized

    You can't use actions with the move trait.

Attitudes 5

  • Helpful

    An attitude: they want to help you and take on reasonable Requests that don't hurt their own goals or way of life. Hostile acts against them sour it.

  • Friendly

    An attitude: they like you and will say yes to simple, safe Requests that don't cost them much. Hostile acts against them sour it.

  • Indifferent

    An attitude: they don't care about you either way. Every creature starts here unless told otherwise.

  • Unfriendly

    An attitude: they dislike and distrust you, and refuse your Requests.

  • Hostile

    An attitude: they want to harm you, though not always with a weapon, and refuse your Requests. Only magic can make a PC hostile.

Objects 1

  • Broken

    Objects only: at or below its Broken Threshold, an item can't do its job or give its bonuses. Broken armor still gives its item bonus to AC, with a −1 (light), −2 (medium), or −3 (heavy) status penalty to AC, and keeps its drawbacks.
